comparison: Perfect agreement on C19 and C21 regarding the reporter strain resource. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers recognize this as a valuable contribution, with OpenEval noting documentation in Supplementary file 1 and Figure 1B, while peer reviewers describe it as helping researchers examine synapse patterning.

Perfect agreement on C36-C40 regarding sexual dimorphism findings. Both evaluations find these claims well-supported. OpenEval cites Figure 3 data with statistical significance, while peer reviewers describe this as 'rigorous experiments' demonstrating the pipeline's utility for measuring sex differences.

Perfect agreement on C47 regarding cytoplasmic markers. Both evaluations support this claim. OpenEval references Figure 4—figure supplement 1B showing improved segmentation accuracy, while peer reviewers explicitly praise this as 'a powerful and useful approach.'

Perfect agreement on C56-C58 regarding developmental synapse scaling in CNS neurons. Both evaluations find these claims convincingly demonstrated. OpenEval cites quantitative measurements in Figure 8, while peer reviewers describe the findings as 'convincingly demonstrated' utility of the pipeline.

Strong agreement on C41, C43, and C48 regarding RAB-3 reporter limitations. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval references Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and protein function studies, while peer reviewers acknowledge these as 'realistically discussed' weaknesses and caveats.

Strong agreement on C46 and C53 regarding pipeline validation against manual quantification. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval cites Figures 4-6 with statistical tests, while peer reviewers confirm the pipeline 'accurately quantitate fluorescent puncta, at least as well as human experimenters.'

Strong agreement on C44-C45 regarding GRASP/iBLINC variability. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval references Figure 5 and previous reports, while peer reviewers accept this as part of 'realistically discussed' weaknesses and appropriate scientific caution.

Strong agreement on C20, C22-C23, C29-C32 regarding WormPsyQi pipeline architecture. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes documentation in methods and figures with U-Net architecture details, while peer reviewers praise the pipeline as 'rigorously validated' with 'significant potential.' Peer review R1 also covers C33-C35, C89-C90, and C92 not in OpenEval R4.

Strong agreement on C63-C65 regarding non-proportional synapse scaling in pharyngeal neurons. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval cites Figure 9B-D showing contrast with CNS neurons, while peer reviewers accept this as part of 'convincingly demonstrated' neuron-to-neuron heterogeneity. Peer review R6 also covers C66 and C68.

Agreement on C72-C73 regarding proportional synapse volume scaling during development. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval references Figure 10D-E with quantitative analysis, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the pipeline's capability to quantify spatial features. Peer review R7 also covers C69 and C71.

Agreement on C69 and C71 regarding spatial synapse distribution patterns. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval cites Figure 10A-C with probability density measurements matching EM observations, while peer reviewers accept this as demonstration of the pipeline's capabilities for spatial analyses.

Agreement on C79-C81 regarding pipeline limitations. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes honest assessment based on testing with various reporters (Figures 4, 6), while peer reviewers view the acknowledgment of limitations as a strength, with authors describing 'potential solutions users can take.' Peer review R11 also covers C75-C76 and C78.

Agreement on C75-C76 regarding transgenic approach limitations. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of potential artifacts and variability, while peer reviewers state 'Weaknesses and caveats are realistically discussed' and view this as a manuscript strength.

Agreement on C33-C35 regarding pipeline performance validation. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval cites Figure 2C-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 4E with IoU scores and processing time comparisons, while peer reviewers describe the validation as 'convincing studies' and 'rigorously validated.'

Agreement on C68 regarding distinct synapse addition patterns between pharyngeal and somatic neurons. Both evaluations support this claim. OpenEval references comparative analysis of Figures 8 and 9, while peer reviewers accept this as part of 'convincingly demonstrated' neuron-to-neuron heterogeneity.

Agreement on C66 regarding proportional synapse addition in specific pharyngeal neurons. Both evaluations support this claim. OpenEval cites Figure 9E-F with interpretation based on EM studies, while peer reviewers accept this as part of demonstrated developmental heterogeneity.

Agreement on C78 regarding future improvements to reporter toolkit. Both evaluations support this claim. OpenEval notes it's supported by general knowledge of C. elegans transgenic approaches, while peer reviewers accept this as part of realistic discussion of limitations and potential solutions.

Agreement on C77 regarding transgenic variability limitations. Both evaluations support this claim. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of limitations, while peer reviewers accept this as part of 'realistically discussed' weaknesses and appropriate scientific caution.

Agreement on C89-C90, C92 regarding methodological details and reproducibility. Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval notes clear documentation and software/data availability statements, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these through their validation of the pipeline's rigor and reproducibility.

OpenEval found C1-C5 regarding prior C. elegans connectomics work well-supported by citations to EM reconstruction studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/context claims.
OpenEval found C6-C8 regarding knowledge gaps in the field well-supported and establishing motivation for the work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these motivational claims.

OpenEval found C54-C55 regarding dauer stage differences well-supported by Figure 7 data with statistical significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific experimental findings.
OpenEval found C59-C60 accurately citing Witvliet et al., 2021 for developmental context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these citation-based contextual claims.
OpenEval found C61-C62 well-supported by citations providing context for pharyngeal neuron development. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval found C74 well-supported by citations to recent studies providing context for stereotyped synapse patterns. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this contextual claim.

OpenEval rated C24 as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation about broader applications without validation data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this speculative claim about future applications.

OpenEval found C25-C28 regarding manual quantification limitations well-supported by citations and practical experience. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological motivation claims.
